Question:
The volume contraction of a solid copper cube, when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of 7×10^6 Pa , would be ____ mm^3 .
(Given bulk modulus of copper =1.4×10^11Nm^(−2) )

text:
To find the volume contraction ($\Delta V$) of the solid copper cube, we use the formula for Bulk Modulus ($B$):

$$B = \frac{P}{\Delta V / V} \implies \Delta V = \frac{P \cdot V}{B}$$

*(Note: The side length of the cube is omitted in the question text, but this is a standard NCERT problem where the edge length of the cube is $L = 10\text{ cm} = 0.1\text{ m}$.)*

1. Volume of the cube: $V = L^3 = (0.1\text{ m})^3 = 10^{-3}\text{ m}^3$
2. Hydraulic pressure: $P = 7 \times 10^6\text{ Pa}$
3. Bulk modulus: $B = 1.4 \times 10^{11}\text{ N m}^{-2}$

Calculating $\Delta V$:
$$\Delta V = \frac{7 \times 10^6 \times 10^{-3}}{1.4 \times 10^{11}} = 5 \times 10^{-8}\text{ m}^3$$

Converting to $\text{mm}^3$ ($1\text{ m}^3 = 10^9\text{ mm}^3$):
$$\Delta V = 5 \times 10^{-8} \times 10^9\text{ mm}^3 = 50\text{ mm}^3$$

# Standard problem: A solid copper cube of edge 10 cm (0.1 m) is subjected to hydraulic pressure of 7 x 10^6 Pa.
# Bulk modulus B = 1.4 x 10^11 N/m^2.
# Let's check: B = P / (dV / V) => dV = P * V / B

P = 7e6 # Pa
B = 1.4e11 # N/m^2

# If L = 10 cm = 0.1 m:
V = (0.1)**3 # 10^-3 m^3
dV_m3 = P * V / B
dV_mm3 = dV_m3 * 1e9

print(f"If L = 10 cm: dV = {dV_mm3} mm^3")
# NCERT Chapter 9 exercise problem:
# "The volume contraction of a solid copper cube of edge 10 cm, when subjected to a hydraulic pressure of 7 \times 10^6 Pa is ..."
# Volume V = (0.1 m)^3 = 10^-3 m^3 = 10^6 mm^3
# Bulk modulus B = 1.4 * 10^11 Pa
# \Delta V = V * P / B = 10^-3 * 7*10^6 / (1.4*10^11) = 7*10^3 / 1.4*10^11 = 5 * 10^-8 m^3
# 5 * 10^-8 m^3 = 5 * 10^-8 * 10^9 mm^3 = 50 mm^3.

print(50)
